question.text: A long straddle with 20 lots at strike 83.00 (call premium 0.20, put premium 0.15). At expiry, USDINR = 82.20. Total P&L?

explanation.text: The Logic: At expiry USDINR 82.20 is below the 83.00 strike, so the call expires worthless: call payoff is zero, less the 0.20 call premium paid. The put is in the money: put payoff = 83.00 - 82.20 = 0.80, less the 0.15 put premium paid, giving a net put payoff of 0.65. Net straddle profit per unit = 0.65 - 0.20 = 0.45 (equivalently, 0.80 - 0.35 total premium = 0.45). Total = 20 lots x 1,000 units x 0.45 = Rs. 9,000. The Trap: Profit of Rs. 16,000 only nets the put premium (0.80 - 0.15 = 0.65) and forgets the 0.20 call premium that was also paid. The loss and Rs. 2,000 figures ignore that the put is deeply in the money at expiry. Note: Explanation rewritten to repair the broken sentence after "Call expires worthless (82.20" and to spell out the per-leg payoff components.
